claims.text: Machine-learning-guided compositional and processing adjustments will enable formation of a more stable and adherent oxide scale.
A more stable and adherent oxide scale will enhance oxidation resistance relative to traditionally processed materials.
The target material is a generic metal or alloy lacking a pre-existing protective oxide barrier and prone to oxidation.
A data-driven machine-learning model can determine compositional descriptors and processing parameters that stabilize a protective oxide scale.
Oxidation is accelerated under the stated ambient-to-elevated-temperature conditions.
A uniform, adherent, and chemically compatible oxide scale impedes oxygen diffusion into the substrate.
Historical oxidation data combined with composition and processing parameters can be used to predict beneficial material modifications.
The predicted modifications promote microstructural changes that lead to a robust oxide scale.
ML-guided materials will exhibit reduced oxidation kinetics compared with conventionally processed controls.
ML-guided materials will exhibit slower oxide growth than conventionally processed controls.
ML-guided materials will exhibit better oxide-scale adherence than conventionally processed controls.
The approach is expected to be effective only when ample historical oxidation data are available.
Predictive reliability may be limited for novel alloy chemistries and highly cyclic thermal conditions.
Reproducibility of the ML predictions across different alloy systems is uncertain.
Long-term stability of the engineered oxide scales under variable service conditions is uncertain.
Weight gain over time can be used to assess oxidation kinetics.
